items.summary: The November 2026 DB-Engines rankings are out. PostgreSQL is the only database in the top four whose line is going up and to the right. Oracle, MySQL and Microsoft SQL Server all lost points this month, and all three are down from a year ago. PostgreSQL gained points on both counts. It now sits just 3.84 points behind SQL Server for third place. On the past year's trend, PostgreSQL could move ahead of SQL Server as early as next month. So it's time to celebrate, right? items.summary: In 2014, if you wanted Postgres servers on several continents, each of them accepting writes and all of them sharing their rows, there was one serious open source answer: BDR, from 2ndQuadrant. It needed a patched PostgreSQL 9.4 and a plugin, which means it needed a server that was not Postgres. Ten years of work on logical replication have since moved most of what BDR needed into the stock server, and in this article we build the same kind of system with Postgres 19 release candidate 1 and pg_auto_failover, to see how far that incremental progress has taken us, and what is still left to build. This is the last article of a series on logical…
